title: Marijuana  Prohibition And the Drug War. A Simple Question of Priorities and Lost Opportunities

content_html_sanitized:
In 2023, the last year for which we have US arrest data, roughly 25% of all drug arrests were for marijuana.

From NORML See FBI: Nearly One Quarter of All Drug-Related Arrests Are for Marijuana Possession

 

In 2023, there were 105,007 drug overdose deaths, of course none were reported as resulting from cannabis, according to the U.S. Government data.

 

A simple question, how many lives might have been saved if the resources that were wasted on marijuana prohibition had instead been used on helping opioid addicts, or arresting opioid smugglers?

 

For obvious reasons, I have tended to focus on the injustices inherent in cannabis prohibition, but we must also remind our politicians and ourselves that law enforcement and justice systems and public health resources are finite.

 

Then there is the problem of the Black Market. Cannabis prohibition is a subsidy to organized crime, which is deeply entrenched in the “marijuana” business. In fact, prohibition is the reason that we call it by a Mexican slang term.

 

Virtually everything negative about cannabis is a result of prohibition. Had cannabis, which was only hemp, been allowed to enter the culture naturally, it would have been promoted in an entirely different way.

 

It would have been promoted as an “herbal remedy” at a time when “medicine” was just getting organized. It would have been used by cancer patients, veterans, and chronic pain patients, at a time when the average person had less money, less access to hospitals.

See Cannabis Prohibition and the Suppression of CBD

 

While the average potency per unit would have increased as our knowledge increased, it would have been understood from the beginning and not glamorized.

See The Perils of Potent Pot Party Line: Blaming Marijuana Legalization for Increase in THC Levels

 

Jazz musicians would still have known That Reefer Man, but there also would have been an alternative to alcohol.

See Legalizing Alcohol Made Under Age Drinking Less Dangerous. Legal Cannabis Can Do The Same for Teens Illegally Toking and Vaping. The Dangers of Synthetic Cannabinoids

 

If the Drug War had still been pursued in exactly the same way, but without cannabis, there would not have been a huge distribution system readymade for cocaine, and the methamphetamines, and heroin, and all the other opiates. Etc.

See HOW THE NARCS CREATED CRACK: The Iron Law of Prohibition Original Article and MarijuanaNews References. In The Time of Fentanyl and Nitazenes

 

And there wouldn’t have been the huge cultural divisions that Nixon promoted to support the Vietnam War. And there wouldn’t have been 30 million arrests.

Just When It Looked Like Marijuana Was About to Be Legalized, What Happened In The 1970s? Life Magazine In 1969!

 

But other than that….
